title: Finite residue field points are closed in finite-type fibres
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $x\in X$ map to $s\in S$, and let $X_s$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. If $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(x)$ is a finite field extension, meaning that $\kappa(x)$ is finite-dimensional as a $\kappa(s)$-vector space [def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension], then the point of $X_s$ induced by $x$ is closed in $X_s$.

source.place: Tags 01TE and 01TF: Tag 01TE proves that an algebraic residue-field extension makes the point closed in its fibre; the stated finite extension is algebraic (Tag 01TF gives the converse under locally finite type).

proof.text: Put T=X_s and let ξ be the point of T induced by x. By stability of locally finite type under base change, the second projection T→Spec κ(s) is locally of finite type. To prove that ξ is closed, let y be any specialization of ξ in T and choose an affine open U⊂T containing y. Opens are stable under generalization, so U also contains ξ.

source.place: Tags 01TE and 01TF: the affine-local proof that algebraic (hence finite) residue extensions make a point closed in the fibre, with the locally-finite-type converse.

proof.text: The restriction U→Spec κ(s) is of finite type: the affine-pair criterion gives a finitely generated κ(s)-algebra for its coordinate ring, and the affine source is quasi-compact. The fibre stalk quotient identifies the local ring of ξ in T with the quotient of the local ring of x by the maximal ideal of κ(s), hence identifies κ_T(ξ) with κ_X(x) and its κ(s)-map. The open immersion U→T preserves this residue field by residue-field naturality. Therefore κ_U(ξ) is finite over κ(s), and the finite-type-over-a-field closed-point criterion makes ξ closed in U.

source.place: Tags 01TE and 01TF: the affine-local proof that algebraic (hence finite) residue extensions make a point closed in the fibre, with the locally-finite-type converse.

proof.text: Since y lies in U and in the closure of {ξ} in T, while ξ is closed in U, we get y=ξ. Thus ξ has no proper specialization. For a scheme this is equivalent to the singleton {ξ} being closed, so the point induced by x is closed in X_s.
